To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the duality of gaze, i.e., the ability to extract and signal social attentional information, is a critical aspect of human social interaction.
the eyes of humans signal social information and that the nature of that information is shaped by social context, e.g., whether the interaction is cooperative or competitive.

the eyes of others are not simply cues for attentional orienting; rather they are the focus of a complex non-verbal communication system in which the eyes both extract and signal social and emotional information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the social attention system in humans, and how it is shaped by the social context in which it operates.
the duality of gaze and its importance for human social interaction.
the role of the eyes of the other in social interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the eyes of others are both an attentional cue and a communication channel, and that the information that they convey depends upon the relationship between individuals.
the duality of gaze has been demonstrated experimentally for the first time and that it has a profound impact on the nature of social interaction.
gaze is a powerful and complex form of social communication that can only be fully understood in the context of the relationship between individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the eyes of humans do not only extract social information, but also signal information to others.
the eyes of others are not simply cues that direct our attention, but also signals that we use to communicate to those others.
the eyes are not only a window to the soul, but also a window to the mind.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to take great care when using schematic images of faces and photos of people to study social attention.
the eyes of others are not merely attentional cues; they are the means by which we communicate with one another.
the eyes of others are both a source and a signal of information, and that the nature of that information depends on the context in which it is being exchanged.
